recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed unless PA revisits the later FHIR-44895 decision about where the Patient Gender and Sex link should appear.
issue_request: FHIR-16453 was Published/Persuasive for FHIR-core Patient and asked to apply tracker 14754 in R4: remove "Gender of individual drives many clinical processes" from Patient.gender requirements and add a Patient Gender section pointer to Patient.gender comments.
initial_application: Commit c407909a65666cce8ff7125b52f3bd7a2f95f47b explicitly named GF#14754 and GF#16453 and changed the old Patient spreadsheet to remove the clinical-process sentence and add the Patient Gender and Sex pointer to the Patient.gender comment. Later source conversion in 33b409a4b6d544598262f2f074ebb4b6dc466157 moved Patient into source/patient/structuredefinition-Patient.xml while preserving the cleaned requirements/comment lineage.
additional_context: Patient is active in source/fhir.ini. The current Patient Gender and Sex section remains in source/patient/patient-notes.xml and later sex-and-gender work such as FHIR-29673 refreshed it. FHIR-44895 later changed where the visibility link should appear: PA minutes record that the proposed short-display placement was not possible with tooling, so the link was put in the Patient.gender definition instead of the comment and PA agreed.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. Current build-scope source has no occurrence of the removed clinical-process sentence; Patient.gender remains administrative; and the Patient Gender and Sex guidance is linked from the Patient.gender definition. Adding the same pointer back to the comment would duplicate guidance and partially undo the later FHIR-44895 placement decision.
